items.title: What Most People Get Wrong About Evolution | Akarsh Kumar
items.summary: A lot of people in AI treat evolution as a dumb fallback, basically random search for when you can't take a gradient. Akarsh Kumar thinks that is wrong. Selection hangs on to partial solutions, so mutations only need to be useful about 1% of the time for the search to keep making progress. Akarsh is a PhD student at MIT working with Phillip Isola, works with Sakana AI, and is first author of the Fractured Entangled Representation paper with Kenneth Stanley, Jeff Clune and Joel Lehman. He tells Tim Scarfe why the path a learner takes may shape the structure of what it learns, and why that is a different way of looking at intelligence from the statistical one. Most of the conversation is about ASAL, the method he led for searching whole spaces of artificial worlds. Rather than predict what a rule will do, ASAL runs the simulation and asks a foundation model what happened. Mapped across all 262,144 Life-like rules, the most interesting worlds sit on one small island. Along the way: Game of Life, Lenia (with a clip from its creator, Bert Chan), neural cellular automata, Boids, Particle Life and the emergence of persistence. The last stretch is Core War, a programming game from the 1980s. Asked cold, LLMs write poor Redcode. Used as the mutation step in an evolutionary loop with a verifier, they produced warriors that, between them, beat or tied 96% of 294 human-written ones. Over repeated rounds the warriors trended towards generalists. --- TIMESTAMPS: 00:00:00 Intro: artificial life, ASAL and Core War in four minutes 00:04:19 Life as it could be, not just as it is A lot of people in AI treat evolution as a dumb fallback, basically random search for when you can't take a gradient. Akarsh Kumar thinks that is wrong. Selection hangs on to partial solutions, so mutations only need to be useful about 1% of the time for the search to keep making progress.

Akarsh is a PhD student at MIT working with Phillip Isola, works with Sakana AI, and is first author of the Fractured Entangled Representation paper with Kenneth Stanley, Jeff Clune and Joel Lehman. He tells Tim Scarfe why the path a learner takes may shape the structure of what it learns, and why that is a different way of looking at intelligence from the statistical one.

Most of the conversation is about ASAL, the method he led for searching whole spaces of artificial worlds. Rather than predict what a rule will do, ASAL runs the simulation and asks a foundation model what happened. Mapped across all 262,144 Life-like rules, the most interesting worlds sit on one small island. Along the way: Game of Life, Lenia (with a clip from its creator, Bert Chan), neural cellular automata, Boids, Particle Life and the emergence of persistence.

The last stretch is Core War, a programming game from the 1980s. Asked cold, LLMs write poor Redcode. Used as the mutation step in an evolutionary loop with a verifier, they produced warriors that, between them, beat or tied 96% of 294 human-written ones. Over repeated rounds the warriors trended towards generalists.

items.title: How to Connect Etsy and Printify to Claude or ChatGPT (Playground Sandbox Setup)
items.summary: Set up Playground Sandbox step by step: connect your Etsy shop and Printify account to Claude or ChatGPT so you can research, design and list print on demand products from one chat. This tutorial covers both the Claude setup and the ChatGPT setup, then runs a first prompt. Written version of every step: https://playgroundai.com/blog/how-to-connect-playground-to-claude-or-chatgpt#connect-playground-to-chatgpt Open Sandbox: https://playgroundai.com WHAT YOU NEED - A Playground account (this is the connection hub and your design tool) - A Printify account - An Etsy shop - Claude or ChatGPT (pick one and stick with it) STEP 1: CONNECT ETSY Log in to Etsy. At playgroundai.com open Sandbox, then Connectors, and click Connect next to Etsy. STEP 2: CONNECT PRINTIFY Click Connect next to Printify. In a new tab go to printify.com/app/account/api, click Generate, name the token (for example "Playground Connection"), keep all scopes and generate it. Copy the token, paste it into Playground and click Connect. Treat the token like a password and don't share it. STEP 3 FOR CLAUDE Copy the MCP server URL from the Connectors page. In Claude open Settings, then Connectors, then Add custom connector. Name it Playground, paste the URL, click Add, then Connect, and log in to Playground. STEP 3 FOR CHATGPT Copy the MCP server URL from the Connectors page. In ChatGPT open Settings, then Plugins, then Browse plugins. Click the plus sign to create a plugin, paste the URL and wait for the confirmation. STEP 4: YOUR FIRST PROMPT "Create three new designs in Playground for the homeschool mom niche. Pull from the templates I have favorited in Playground." Your designs appear on your Board in Playground as they're made. Set up Playground Sandbox step by step: connect your Etsy shop and Printify account to Claude or ChatGPT so you can research, design and list print on demand products from one chat. This tutorial covers both the Claude setup and the ChatGPT setup, then runs a first prompt.

Written version of every step: https://playgroundai.com/blog/how-to-connect-playground-to-claude-or-chatgpt#connect-playground-to-chatgpt
Open Sandbox: https://playgroundai.com

WHAT YOU NEED
- A Playground account (this is the connection hub and your design tool)
- A Printify account
- An Etsy shop
- Claude or ChatGPT (pick one and stick with it)

STEP 1: CONNECT ETSY
Log in to Etsy. At playgroundai.com open Sandbox, then Connectors, and click Connect next to Etsy.

STEP 2: CONNECT PRINTIFY
Click Connect next to Printify. In a new tab go to printify.com/app/account/api, click Generate, name the token (for example "Playground Connection"), keep all scopes and generate it. Copy the token, paste it into Playground and click Connect. Treat the token like a password and don't share it.

STEP 3 FOR CLAUDE
Copy the MCP server URL from the Connectors page. In Claude open Settings, then Connectors, then Add custom connector. Name it Playground, paste the URL, click Add, then Connect, and log in to Playground.

STEP 3 FOR CHATGPT
Copy the MCP server URL from the Connectors page. In ChatGPT open Settings, then Plugins, then Browse plugins. Click the plus sign to create a plugin, paste the URL and wait for the confirmation.

STEP 4: YOUR FIRST PROMPT
"Create three new designs in Playground for the homeschool mom niche. Pull from the templates I have favorited in Playground."
Your designs appear on your Board in Playground as they're made.
